classification.difficultyReason: Match eight graphical inequalities to intervals, distinguishing strict endpoints, poles, square-root domains and absolute-value comparisons with variable right-hand sides.

inlines.text: Match the question with the solution set.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x-4|$ and $y=1$. They intersect at $x=3$ and $x=5$. The V-shaped graph is above the line outside these points. Strict inequality excludes both endpoints.

$x<3$ or $x>5$.

Correct answer: (a).

spec.description: Equation-driven absolute-value graph and horizontal line with open comparison endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Intersections (3,1) and (5,1); blue above red for x<3 or x>5.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\dfrac{2}{x-3}$ and $y=1$. The vertical asymptote is $x=3$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{x-3}&=1\\2&=x-3\\x&=5\end{align*}$$

The rational graph is on or below the line for $x<3$ or $x\geq5$. Exclude the pole and include the intersection.

Correct answer: (b).

spec.description: Rational graph and horizontal line with dashed pole and included equality point.
spec.mathematics: Pole x=3; intersection (5,1); blue on or below red for x<3 or x>=5.

answer.short:
(c): $(-\infty,3]\cup(5,\infty)$.

Compare the V-shaped graph with the rational graph; $x=5$ is excluded.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x-4|$ and $y=\dfrac{2}{5-x}$, with vertical asymptote $x=5$. On the branch $x\leq4$, their intersection satisfies

$$\begin{align*}(4-x)(5-x)&=2\\x^2-9x+18&=0\\(x-3)(x-6)&=0\end{align*}$$

Only $x=3$ belongs to this branch. There is no intersection for $4<x<5$, since $(x-4)(5-x)\leq\dfrac14<2$. For $x>5$, the rational graph is negative and the absolute-value graph is nonnegative.

The absolute-value graph is on or above the rational graph for $x\leq3$ or $x>5$. Include $x=3$ and exclude the pole.

Correct answer: (c).

spec.description: Equation-driven absolute-value and rational graphs with included intersection and excluded pole.
spec.mathematics: Unique intersection (3,1); pole x=5; solution x<=3 or x>5.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|2x-7|$ and $y=x-2$. On the left branch, $7-2x=x-2$ gives $x=3$. On the right branch, $2x-7=x-2$ gives $x=5$.

The V-shaped graph is on or above the line for $x\leq3$ or $x\geq5$. Equality includes both endpoints.

Correct answer: (d).

spec.description: Absolute-value graph and increasing straight line with two included intersections.
spec.mathematics: Intersections (3,1) and (5,3); blue on or above red outside the interval between them.

answer.worked:
Sketch the upper semicircle $y=\sqrt{4-(x-4)^2}$, with domain $2\leq x\leq6$, and the line $y=\sqrt3$.

$$\begin{align*}4-(x-4)^2&=3\\(x-4)^2&=1\\x&=3,\ 5\end{align*}$$

The semicircle is above the line for $3<x<5$. Strict inequality excludes both intersections.

Correct answer: (e).

spec.description: Upper semicircle of radius 2 centred at (4,0) and a horizontal comparison line.
spec.mathematics: Domain [2,6]; intersections x=3 and x=5; strict solution (3,5). Parametric semicircle retains equal axis units.

answer.worked:
Sketch the upper semicircle $y=\sqrt{1-(x-4)^2}$, with domain $3\leq x\leq5$, and the line $y=x-5$.

Throughout $3\leq x<5$, the semicircle is nonnegative and the line is negative, so the semicircle lies above the line. At $x=5$, both equal zero and strict inequality fails. At $x=3$, $0>-2$, so the domain endpoint is included.

Correct answer: (f).

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle centred at (4,0) and increasing line, with included left domain endpoint and excluded right equality endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Domain [3,5]; strict inequality holds on [3,5). Equal axis units preserve the semicircle.

answer.short:
(g): $(-\infty,1]\cup(3,5]$.

Compare both branches; include $x=1,5$ and exclude $x=3$.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\dfrac4{x-3}$ and $y=x-3$, excluding $x=3$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac4{x-3}&=x-3\\4&=(x-3)^2\\x&=1,\ 5\end{align*}$$

For $x<3$, the rational graph is on or above the line when $x\leq1$. For $x>3$, it is on or above the line when $3<x\leq5$.

The complete solution is $(-\infty,1]\cup(3,5]$. Include both equality points and exclude the pole.

Correct answer: (g).

spec.description: Rational graph and line showing both equality intersections and the excluded pole.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\sqrt{1-(x-4)^2}$ and $y=|x-4|-1$. The square root restricts the domain to $3\leq x\leq5$.

On this domain, the semicircle is nonnegative and $|x-4|-1\leq0$. The semicircle is therefore on or above the V-shaped graph throughout the domain, with equality at $x=3$ and $x=5$.

Correct answer: (h).

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle and absolute-value graph, with both common domain endpoints included.
spec.mathematics: Domain [3,5]; semicircle on or above the V-shaped graph throughout its domain. Equal axis units preserve the semicircle.
